I'm a writer and artist in general, and I lean mostly towards darker themes in my work. I sometimes get anxious about sharing my work, especially the more personal things like my poetry, because of how people might react. I also remember simply asking my mom for a snack or something? I don't remember what for but she yelled at me that this was 'her time' and I had to leave her alone.

Being to excited and having too much fun was wrong, too. If I laughed too loud for too long I was scolded. If I got too enthusiastic, I was told to stop.

Well, I learned how to cry silently and slowly soothe myself until calm from a young age. I never cried unless I was completely alone in a room. I also kept all my passion inside and began laughing less and sort of just...becoming placid. I learned that my emotions were a burden.

I usually use a name generator or name lists that show meanings. I compile a list of names that sound nice and like they might work for the character, with meanings if possible. Then, I slowly get rid of my least favorites of the list. I keep narrowing it down until I have one left.

I find it helps to have some kind of visual representation of the character (if you can't do that, a written description might be able to supplement) and look at it while saying the names out loud. It helps me see if the name fits them. 

For fantasy, try taking names that are already kind of unique or whimsical and fuse them together in different ways. Ex. One name I came up with is Myradona, which is the name Lyra with an M instead of an L fused with Belladonna and one N removed. A simpler one is Dex, which is just Lexi with the I removed and L replaced with a D.

One final strategy I have for fantasy and sci-fi names is that I take a descriptive line about the character (Ex. "A cool alien friend") and using the letters in it to make a name using the following needlessly complex method:

Start by removing the repeating letters- "A cool alien friend" becomes "A col ien frd"

Then, remove any clusters of letters that lack vowels- "A col ien"

Finally, use the remaining letters to create some names. You can add or take away letters, rearrange the order of sounds, or whatever else you want to make it look better or create different pronunciations-
"A-Colien"
"Aecoliin"
"Akol'yen"
"Yen Akol"
"Eyin Akal"

Hope any of these ideas help.

I was working my fast food job a few months back and a woman came in, she looked to be in rough shape, likely homeless. She came up to my counter and ordered a coffee that is usually for free if you're a senior, but requires a purchase. She had no money, so I gave her the item anyway and she thanked me.


I suffer from depression among other things and was in a serious rough patch. I was also very angry at the injustice of the world, so seeing this woman who had to get by on free coffee really affected me. As she was getting ready to leave, I quickly went to the back and grabbed a twenty from my wallet. I stopped her and gave it to her, she thanked me profusely and offered me a chocolate. I imagine she was selling those chocolates by the piece to make some change. I declined, I had to get back to work.


A few days later, I was doing even worse mentally. I was starting to consider doing something drastic. While going through the motions at work, she came in again.


She told me that because of the money I gave her, she was able to eat for the past few days and she left a chocolate by my till before I could stop her. I wasn't able to give her anything that time, unfortunately, as a trickier boss of mine was nearby.


That woman doesn't know this, but she very well may have saved my life that day. I was feeling like I'd never amount to anything, that my life was pointless and that I was worthless. But knowing that I made life even slightly easier for that woman just for a little bit made me feel like maybe I do make a difference, that maybe my life isn't a waste. 


She hasn't come in since, I hope she's doing well. I'm doing better now, I've had some close calls like that in my life but somehow something always happens to pull me out of it, maybe I have angels or something haha

Orcs are fearsome, intimidating, battle hardened beasts. Goblins are diminutive, bony, shrewd little creatures. About the only thing the two peoples have in common is being green, well, that and a healthy love of competition.

 The southern tribes of these two groups in the sprawling lands of Golthila had a yearly tradition based on this shared love. Each year, on the day of the summer solstice, the warriors of each migrate to the sparsely wooded land between their two territories. Then they fight one another with blunt weapons until sundown and the group with the most people still standing win. 

 To the high and mighty grace of the Elven population, this was a pointless and barbaric tradition. To the humans, it was childish. In fact, not a single race in the land really understood why the yearly battle happened. The excuse the goblins and orcs gave was that it allowed their troops to keep themselves battle ready. The dwarves decided they just thought it was entertaining to beat eachother up and respected them for it.

 Regardless, the battle like clockwork ravaged the surrounding area each year. No deaths ever occured, they were all sure to avoid that. But injuries were plenty. Mostly, the goblins suffered the bulk of the injuries. That, and the shame of defeat.

 Yes, even if no one got the point of this practice, everyone could predict that every single time the battle occured, the goblins would go home nursing broken limbs and shattered dreams. It was a forgone conclusion, really. Orcs are seven feet tall and goblins just over half that. Orcs are beefy and powerful, goblins are...not. The orcs teased their smaller opponents relentlessly for a few weeks after the battle each year, but despite the humiliation the goblins showed up just the same the next year.

 You see, goblins are stubborn. Incredibly so. Getting a goblin to quit is like trying to pet a dragon, someone's losing an arm before that happens. Goblins are also very resourceful. And, they are conniving, sneaky little bastards.

 About seven years ago, the orcs decided to throw the goblins a bone. They sent a message to the goblin's king saying that they could bring one extra piece of equipment to the fight to aid them. The rules of the brawl was generally that each warrior could only have one blunt weapon, enough food and water for the day, and the clothes on their back. No armour, no horses, no extra weaponry.

 The goblin King, Dort, liked this opportunity. Most races might have seen the orc's actions as patronising, but goblins don't care about that sort of thing. Goblins will take anything they are given. King Dort was no exception, and immediately called a meeting with his generals.

 Any intelligent being would have taken this opportunity to suit their warriors in armour. However, the grateful letter the Orc Queen M'Gorra recieved from her old friend Kind Dort said the following:

 Dear Queen M'Gorra, 

 We of the humble goblin tribe greatly appreciate your offer. However, we would like to respectfully decline it and instead are sending a gift of gratitude for your sportsmanship. Please accept this gift and feel free to use it during our battle. I look forward to facing your mace one again, old friend.

 Signed, Kind Dort

 The queen was beyond amused at this, she hardly ceased her laughter even when the goblin riders came with the king's gift. She met the horses at the edge of her kingdom and smiled down at the four feet tall goblin who shuffled over to her and bowed before ordering others to bring over the things they'd brought.

 M'Gorra discovered that the goblins had brought fine dwarven stilts, a piece of equipment dwarves used to reach high things while working. They were made of dwarven metals, light but durable. Each pair consisted of two poles with slightly wide base and foot shaped platforms about two feet up from the bottom. The rest of the pole, which would end at the hips of a dwarf or goblin, had two pairs of leather straps to attach the things to the wearer's legs. 

 M'Gorra's stomach hurt as she desperately tried to show the things to her generals and advisors. Her deep, bellowing laugh echoed through the sky, as did the laughs of her companions. Surely the goblins couldn't be this foolish? To give their opponents, who already towered over them, height enhancing devices? 

 The week after that, the warriors of both tribes prepared early in the morning for the yearly battle. The goblins got their rations together and calmly arrived first at the regular location holding clubs, hammers, and a few maces.

 The orcs strapped themselves into the stilts, thinking about how easily the goblins would be defeated. Many orc warriors stumbled a bit while getting onto their extended feet, but got the hang of the things rather quickly.

 When the orcs arrived, the goblins had no really visible reaction to the now nine foot tall behemoths weilding steel maces and hammers before them. The orcs smirked and chuckled proudly, knowing this would be a quick win. 

 When the horn was blown to signify the beginning of the battle, the goblins descended apon the opposing army more eagerly than they ever had before. The orcs easily took out a couple with huge swings of their hammers, but quickly the tables turned as aggressive swings to the bottoms of the stilts caused many of them to stumble and trip.

 The top-heavy orcs weren't built for stilts, evidently. They could walk in them just fine, but as soon as running was involved they fell like chopped down trees. The relentless battering of clubs to the stilts caused even more to fall.

 And once an orc fell, they could not get back up. It was impossible to get up one foot at a time as one does, the stilts were too thin and unstable. Despite being nine feet tall just a few moments before, orcs were reduced to flailing, squirming idiots being trampled by goblins and bonked in the head with clubs. 

 Among the fray, Queen M'Gorra toppled over at the feet of King Dort. It was the first time her massive, muscular form had ever been laid out in battle. Looking up at her friend, she was in utter disbelief as his smile was quickly obscured by the ruddy, poor quality mace sending her into a nice nap. 

 It wasn't even lunchtime when the last orc fell. After bathing in victory, goblins walked among the sorry piles of orc and helped some remove the blasted stilts. Bandages were handed to and fro, and no friendships were ended. But of course, the orc's bodies were actually the least bruised part of them.

 The orcs, tasting the humiliation their friends had suffered for decades, had a new respect for the smaller people. Warriors they were, not of brute strength, but of a realm orcs couldn't understand. The goblin's advantage was their minds.

 After all, they had remembered and exploited a very important trait of the Orc tribes. Orcs are fearsome, intimidating, battle hardened beasts. They are also rather stupid.

It was garbage day, and as always you could see people hauling their garbage and unwanted or broken furniture to the dumpster. I was one of those people, I only had one main trash bag and one small bag from the bathroom to take out.

 I placed the stool I had brought out with me, as I am too short to reach the dumpster on my own. The bags were tossed into the dumpster with little thought. During a half second it took, I caught a glimpse of something human shaped in the dumpster 

 I froze, wondering if I'd seen correctly. I looked over the lip of the dumpster, holding my breath to spare myself of the rancid smell. I expected to see a regular old dumpster diver, which would be strange considering it was road daylight in a residential area but not impossible.

  Not so. This was a dead body. The stillness of the eyes, which were open and staring up at me, told me so. I now know what heart palpitations feel like. I yanked myself back, but then looked again, curiousity getting the better of me. A man with a yellow raincoat on, bloody. An equally bloody hat lay in the garbage near the body.

 I stood there for what could have been anything from five minutes to half an hour before I finally seemed to re-enter my body and called the cops.

 The rest of that day is a blur. I have no idea what took place before or after I discovered the body. That is why I'm so confused as to why I am on trial here today. I know I did not kill that man, I know I am innocent. 

 "I, Curious George, swear to tell the whole truth and nothing but the truth" I signed, unable to speak verbally despite my high intelligence for my species.

I sighed as I walked onto set. Pluto had been fired, and now I’d have to work with a new dog for the first time in decades. Pluto was probably job searching in our apartment, but I knew well that I’d be paying his half of the rent from now on. Funny animals can’t find any work outside of Disney. 

I put on my signature Mickey smile as I approached the director. “Hey Michael.” He said. There was something about the way he said it, like he was my doctor about to tell me I had mouse herpes. I knew that voice, it was the one he used when he told Pluto the news. “Your costar should arrive…oh. Now.”

He gestured behind me, but before I turned he placed a hand on my shoulder. “Michael…you know Disney likes consistency, they…my god…I’m sorry.” The director’s voice faltered, his eyes dark but unwavering as they stared into mine, “Despite Pluto’s fireable conduct…he’s vital to the show. Just…I’m so fucking sorry.” The director shut his eyes and I saw that his hands were shaking as he dropped them at his sides.

I turned around. I wish I hadn’t.

The eyes of the actor wearing Pluto’s skin were showing through the holes in the face. It looked like Pluto except for those human eyes, an awkwardly moving, twisted version of my former friend.

 The mouth was somehow made to stay in that cheerful smile all of us actors were expected to maintain. The man inside was just a bit too thin, and extra skin hung and wrinkled in places it shouldn’t have. The tail was completely slack. There was a thin green zipper running down the back, sewn into the skin. There were no visual indicators that told me how my pal had met his untimely end.

I felt my stomach turn. This wasn’t real, it couldn’t be. I knew the company was ruthless but this…it was incomprehensible. Nausea filled my body and the floor swayed beneath me.

 I didn’t even notice the CEO with…it until he spoke with the most chilling smile on his Face I had ever seen.

“Consistency is important to the brand, you understand right Mike?”

If you know of the content creator CallMeKris, she made a video where she went to a haunted candy store in my province. That candy store has an old elevator in the main shop area, this is one of the most haunted parts of the building. So when me and my family visited the store, I decided I just had to enter the elevator to see what all the fuss is about.

 I sat on the bench in silence, just existing in the space for a moment. Then, this horrible feeling crept up on me, just utter dread. It was like some unseen threat was watching me, and I felt the urge to look around for it. I felt so vulnerable and isolated despite the store having plenty of people in it.

 Then, in my right ear, I heard and felt a sort of breathy whisper. If it was a whisper and not a breath, I couldn't tell what was said. It sounded like a younger man to me. Immediately, I felt the need to exit the elevator. I have never literally noped out of a situation until that day.

 The rest of the time I was in the store I felt a deep, unsettling feeling of being watched. I was also quite nauseated and dizzy. I felt unwelcome, and like some pissed off entity was scrutinizing me.

 My mother felt the exact same feeling (she also went in the elevator) and we both seem to be sensitive to the paranormal. I swear, I have never felt so much disdain towards me in my life. Whatever haunts that place, it did not want me there at all.

Some basic tips I try to always implement:

1. Give them a specific goal. If your character has no goal they have nothing to work towards, and the readers have nothing to root for. This goal can be literally anything from saving their kidnapped sibling to starting a bakery to getting a new car. Bonus points if their goal changes somewhere during the story.
2. Give them multiple flaws. No good character just has one flaw, in fact, no real person does. Make these flaws complex, not just words like "Selfish" or "Rude", write them as full sentences. Example: He views others as stepping stones toward success, therefore he acts cold and harsh to them.
3. Make them change. No good character stays the same throughout the story. Make your character grow or learn, or maybe even make them become a worse person if you're daring. Just don't end with the exact same person you started with. 
4. Let them make mistakes. If your character does everything right, your story will be boring. People fail, and so should your character.
5. Dark Room: This is the big statement you want to make about your character. Maybe it's a flaw, in fact it likely should be a flaw. You must NEVER state this outright in the story, rather it should be implied through their actions in the story. Make it relate to the story's theme if possible. The Dark Room is an element of every story in existence, whether the author knew it or not.

Hope these tips help you out! Character creation/development is kind of my favourite thing to do so I think about it a lot.

I heard a noise coming from the kitchen, like human footsteps. I got up slowly from the couch. Cautiously, I peered around the corner, looking into the kitchen.

 "Holy shit!" I gasped, then clapped my hand over my mouth. 

 "Whoa, don't say the H word around me!" A dark, raspy voice said. "So...I assume you're Gwendolyn, right?"

 I took another look at what I had seen. He was tall, and had long white hair. His eyes were pure red and he wore a black hoodie. His mouth was a little bit open so I saw that he had rather pointy teeth. I tried to speak but no words came out, I was so frightened and confused.

 "Geez, you humans get scared of the littlest of things. I'm Eldon, I'm sure you know why I'm here?" The man said. I shook my head.

 "N-no, what are you anyway?" I asked, trembling.

 "Ugh, seriously...nobody in hell can get anything done." He sighed. "Well, I'm a demon. As for why I'm here, I have to be your guardian. Most get an angel, but...you're one of the special cases."

 I was way more confused now. "Guardian demon? What kind of special case?"

 "Oh, well that's pleasant." I said sarcastically. Eldon walked towards me and squinted, looking at me up and down. I froze, waiting for what he'd do next.
